The stock is below its pre-Q2 close of $2.80 (2026-08-12) after a +42.5% day on that print that it gave back within three sessions (Yahoo daily bars). Front-expiry straddle implies about 23% for the event, but the ATM spread is 67% of mid, so that number is indicative only. view: The Q2 'record' was mostly accounting. Of $14.1m licensing revenue, $8.5m was the present value of a $10m, 30-year content license sold on 2026-06-30 to the buyer of the brands CURI disposed of that same day. That license pays $2.5m a year starting June 2027 (10-Q Note 16). Barter added another $5.3m of non-cash revenue. Without the one-off, Q2 revenue was about $14.7m. That puts H1 2026 underlying revenue near $29.9m, against $34.1m in H1 2025. Operating cash flow was -$4.2m in Q2. Cash and securities fell from $23.4m to $10.9m in one quarter, while the $5m-a-quarter dividend was paid. The CFO left two weeks after the print, filed a Form 144 to sell, and was replaced at a $120k salary. The CEO bought 50k shares at about $2.55-2.60. Management's H2 guide ($38-41m revenue, about $20m of licensing at the low end, year-end cash and investments of $17-22m) needs a large cash licensing inflow that I can find no public trace of. There were no 8-K licensing announcements in Q3 2026, unlike the 2025-10-29 release before last year's +19% print. No 2.03 8-K shows a revolver draw. Arithmetically, Q3-end cash is probably thin and the Q4 dividend, normally declared with this release, is at real risk. Against that, all of this has been public since 2026-08-13 and the price has already fallen about 16% below its pre-Q2 level, to a 14% yield. The release will also carry a non-cash gain from remeasuring the Spiegel stake, and management has shown it will dress the headline ('record'). Past opening prints leaned up on headlines. So the downside story is visible and largely in the price. The open turns on the headline numbers and on whether the dividend survives, and I cannot see either ahead of time. I lean slightly down and do not recommend.

recommendation.reason: The weak points (non-cash Q2 revenue, cash burn, a dividend not covered by operating cash, an aggressive H2 guide) are real and dated. But they have been public since the 10-Q of 2026-08-13 and were written up by aggregators, and the stock has de-rated to a 14% yield and a 52-week low. I cannot show that the price does not already hold a cut. The opening print is driven by a headline that management shapes and that will include a non-cash remeasurement gain.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: The Q4 dividend held at $0.085, with Q3-end cash and investments up from $10.9m because of a named, cash-paying AI licensing deal, would make the 14% yield look wrong and point to a large gap up.

self_critique: The guide was issued on 2026-08-12, after the quarter had started, by a management that knew its pipeline. The year-end cash target suggests a contracted, cash-paying deal that may land in Q3 or Q4. If the Q3 release shows that deal and keeps the dividend, a stock priced for a cut at a 14% yield could gap 25-40%, as on 2025-05-06 and 2026-08-12, and 5 of 7 opens were up. On the other side, a cut plus a revenue shortfall could still take another 15-20% off. My slight down-lean rests on missing evidence (no deal press releases), which is weak.
approach_notes: P4 helped. It made me ask whether the Q2 accounting issue was already priced, and the post-Aug-13 price path and aggregator write-ups showed that it largely was. P3's 'freshest data first' found little for a microcap with no Q3-dated trace, so the view rests on filings and arithmetic.
